findings.text: The first lines tell a newcomer what Athena is in plain words. This is the only description of Athena on the page, though, and the rest is about another project.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The page says why it exists: it is a demonstration. A newcomer can tell that the long firstmate content is a sample of Athena's output, not Athena's own documentation.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but almost all of the page is a deep study of firstmate's states, transitions and claims. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to scroll past dozens of firstmate terms (yolo, secondmate, close-pending, exit 75) that don't help them decide whether to use Athena.
findings.source: Title / h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: A link near the top jumps straight to the next steps, so a reader who doesn't need the study can skip it.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The next steps give a concrete install command and a first command to try. They don't give the clone command or any prerequisites, such as a Rust toolchain or AI model access, so the reader has to go to the GitHub repo to actually begin.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: This passage lists relaunch and secondmate as kinds of task, but elsewhere relaunch is an action (t8) and a secondmate is "not a backlog item". A first-time reader could come away confused about what the task kinds actually are.
findings.source: Start here: "Tasks are handled differently by kind. A ship changes a project; ... A scout produces a report ... A relaunch replaces a stuck worker with a new one. A secondmate is a persistent home, not a backlog item."

findings.text: This wording is awkward: the definitions of agent and code come right after this paragraph and before the cards. "Below the cards' heading" makes the reader look for them in the wrong place.
findings.source: Transitions: "The two deciders are explained below the cards' heading."

findings.text: The page says openly that nothing was run and every claim comes from reading the source. This helps a newcomer judge how far to trust the study.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."
